local_argument_supplements.argument: For zeta monotonicity, write a=sqrt(|kappa|)c. For a>0, (a coth a)'=(sinh a cosh a-a)/sinh(a)^2>=0, since the numerator vanishes at 0 and its derivative is 2 sinh(a)^2>=0. Continuity handles a=0. Thus c<=D implies zeta(kappa,c)<=zeta(kappa,D). For a supporting subgradient g at x with g!=0, take the unit direction v=g/||g|| and y=Exp_x(hv), h>0. On a Hadamard manifold d(x,y)=h; the supporting inequality and global Lipschitzness give h||g||<=f(y)-f(x)<=L_f h, hence ||g||<=L_f; g=0 is immediate. For averaging, bar x_1=x_1 is feasible and satisfies f(bar x_1)=f(x_1). If bar x_s is feasible and f(bar x_s)<=s^(-1)sum_{i=1}^s f(x_i), geodesic convexity of X makes bar x_{s+1} feasible, and that of f gives f(bar x_{s+1})<=(s/(s+1))f(bar x_s)+(1/(s+1))f(x_{s+1})<=(s+1)^(-1)sum_{i=1}^{s+1}f(x_i). Induction proves the required inequality for every t.

proofs.locator: PDF p.9 Theorem 9 Proof Eqs. (8)–(9), completed at top of p.10
map: By the supporting inequality, f(x_s)-f(x*)<=<-g_s,Log_{x_s}(x*)>. Corollary 8, ||g_s||<=L_f and d(x_s,x*)<=D give Eq. (8): f(x_s)-f(x*) <= (d(x_s,x*)^2-d(x_{s+1},x*)^2)/(2 eta)+zeta(kappa,D)L_f^2 eta/2.

Sum from s=1 to t and divide by t. The squared-distance terms telescope, giving Eq. (9); discard the nonpositive terminal term and use d(x_1,x*)<=D. The mean gap is at most D^2/(2t eta)+zeta(kappa,D)L_f^2 eta/2.
Substituting eta=D/(L_f sqrt(zeta(kappa,D)t)) makes the two terms equal and yields D L_f sqrt(zeta(kappa,D)/t).

At the top of PDF p.10 the source invokes geodesic convexity and induction to pass from the mean of function values to the recursive geodesic average; the explicit elementary completion is separated below.

assumptions: Sectional curvature lies in [kappa,0], with finite kappa<=0. The diameter of X is at most D, with D>0.
f:M->R is geodesically convex and L_f-Lipschitz in the sense of Definition 3, with L_f>0; an attained minimizer x* belongs to X, as assumed in section 2.3.

For an arbitrary initial x_1 in X and integer horizon t>=1, use eta=D/(L_f sqrt(zeta(kappa,D)t)). At s=1,...,t query an exact supporting subgradient g_s at x_s and set x_{s+1}=P_X(Exp_{x_s}(-eta g_s)). The source uses ||g_s||<=L_f in Eq. (8).
Set bar x_1=x_1 and, for s>=1, bar x_{s+1}=Exp_{bar x_s}((1/(s+1)) Log_{bar x_s}(x_{s+1})). The output is bar x_t, averaging x_1,...,x_t, rather than bar x_{t+1}.
statement.objects_and_definitions: M is a Hadamard manifold with distance d, Exp and Log; X is nonempty closed and geodesically convex. zeta(kappa,c)=sqrt(|kappa|)c/tanh(sqrt(|kappa|)c), with continuous value 1 at zero argument. Subgradients satisfy f(y)>=f(x)+<g_x,Log_x(y)> for every y in M, as in Definition 1.
statement.parameter_domains: t is a positive integer; D,L_f>0; finite kappa<=0. kappa=0 is interpreted by continuity. Degenerate constant/singleton cases are outside the displayed tuning formula.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every problem satisfying these conditions, every integer t>=1, every initial x_1 in X and every admissible exact subgradient sequence, the horizon-tuned run has the stated deterministic objective-error bound.
